summary.text: Eric Sorensen is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Illinois's 17th District, first elected in 2022 and seeking a third term. He worked for more than two decades as a television meteorologist in Illinois before entering politics, and sits on the House Agriculture and Armed Services committees.

paragraphs.text: Born and raised in Rockford, Illinois, according to his official House biography.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Northern Illinois University (Ballotpedia lists the graduation year inconsistently, so it is omitted here); Wikipedia reports he studied communications and meteorology there and graduated from Boylan Catholic High School.
Began his career as a television meteorologist at KTRE in Lufkin, Texas (1999–2000) and later worked in Tyler, Texas, before serving as chief meteorologist at WREX in Rockford from 2003 to 2014.

Became senior meteorologist at WQAD in the Quad Cities in 2014 and retired from television in 2021; his House biography describes more than two decades as a local TV meteorologist in Central and Northwestern Illinois.
Worked in communications for UnityPoint Health after leaving television and served on the boards of Clock, Inc. and the Project of the Quad Cities.
Announced his candidacy for Congress on November 10, 2021, after Rep. Cheri Bustos said she would not seek re-election, and defeated Republican Esther Joy King in the November 2022 general election.
Took office in January 2023. Re-elected in 2024, defeating Republican Joseph McGraw with 54.4% of the vote, and renominated without opposition in the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary.

In the 119th Congress serves on the House Agriculture Committee and the Armed Services Committee (Readiness, and Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees); in the 118th Congress he served on Agriculture and on Science, Space, and Technology, where he was ranking member of the Space and Aeronautics subcommittee.
Resides in Moline with his partner, Shawn, according to his official House biography.
